In domain management terms, “clientHold” is a standard EPP (Extensible Provisioning Protocol) status code controlled exclusively by the registrar, not by governments or external authorities. According to ICANN documentation and registrar policies, this status instructs the registry not to publish the domain in the DNS, effectively taking it offline until the registrar resolves the underlying issue. Such instruction can be issued only by the owner of the website, not third parties, not even governments. Alternately, the domain provider or the host can take the website offline due to various reasons.

It is commonly applied for routine administrative reasons such as incomplete WHOIS contact verification, billing or payment problems, compliance violations, or at the request of the domain owner. The clientHold affects resolution globally at the registry level, not at any country level.

On the other hand, when a government orders blocking a website, it is done through ISPs (Internet Service Providers) in the country, and the block only takes place in that country. In India, such a block is typically enforced through the Department of Telecommunications via ISP-level DNS poisoning, IP blacklisting, or URL filtering. Such actions allow the domain to still resolve correctly on international resolvers outside the country. That is why websites blocked by the Indian govt can be accessed in India through VPN.

Moreover, when one visits a website blocked by the govt, the browser displays a message saying the same. But when one visits cockroachjantaparty’s website, the browser displays the code DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN. This means the browser can’t find the domain because it has been deactivated.

*STATEMENT: Escalating Digital Censorship in India*

*New Delhi, February 28, 2026*

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) is concerned by a cluster of online blocking and takedown actions and ISP level service disruptions reported between 24–28 February 2026. Across these incidents, users and affected services face restrictions without clear, timely reasons and without access to the underlying orders needed to challenge state action by exercising their rights to obtain legal remedy.

Developers reported severe, uneven disruption in access to Supabase across multiple Indian networks. Reporting indicates the disruption followed a government direction, with accounts suggesting use of Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000. Yet there has been no public statement of the grounds, scope, or duration, and no accessible order for those impacted. Supabase has publicly stated that its domains became inaccessible due to a “ministry order”, and users have been pushed to workarounds such as alternative DNS or VPNs. In parallel, users on X (formerly Twitter) continue to receive “withheld in India” notices restricting specific posts within the country. Such notices usually do not provide the government order or its reasoning. Hence, for those who are being censored the basics of natural justice of a notice, opportunity for a hearing and remedy are delayed or absent.

This is enabled by secrecy built into the blocking framework. Section 69A is implemented through the 2009 Blocking Rules, which contemplate a committee process and, where feasible, notice to intermediaries and identifiable originators. But they also impose “strict confidentiality” over requests and actions taken. When orders and reasons are secret by default, affected persons cannot test legality, necessity, proportionality, or factual errors except through protracted litigation. When in _Shreya Singhal v. Union of India_ (2015), the Supreme Court upheld Section 69A while relying on the existence of procedural safeguards and reasoned decisions, indicating that impacted users could approach court in writ remedies. However, due to the operational secrecy and providing copies of orders and notices those who are censored and prevented from obtaining judicial remedy.

The February 2026 amendments to the IT Rules, 2021 further increase these risks. The substituted Rule 3(1)(d) requires intermediaries to remove or disable access within three hours of receiving “actual knowledge”, which can arise from a court order or a written “reasoned intimation” by authorised government officers. While the rule lists what a “reasoned intimation” should contain, the legal basis, statutory provision, nature of the unlawful act, and specific URL/identifier, the three-hour window pressures platforms to comply promptly which may often occur without any substantive assessment. These inherently opaque censorship practices are being accelerated through "Sahyog" portal. Developed by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), the Sahyog portal operates entirely without statutory footing, only being anchored in the IT Rules, 2021 that are created by executive notification. It functions as a censorship clearinghouse that deliberately bypasses the established, albeit weak, procedural safeguards of Section 69A. By routing automated takedown directives directly to intermediaries under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, the portal structurally excludes citizens and impacted users from the grievance process.

We demand that the government introduce strictly judicially enforceable transparency requirements, publish all blocking orders, and restore the principles of natural justice to India's platform governance framework. Based on requests from our community we will also next week launch a rough public sheet in which social media users can input and add information on digital censorship.

ONE GOVERNMENT BLOCKING ORDER EVERY 68 SECONDS — IS INDIA'S DIGITAL DEMOCRACY UNDER THREAT?

Pause for a moment. In the five months from March to July 2026, nearly 1.95 lakh government-backed blocking orders were sent to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube, according to data reported by The Indian Express.

That is approximately 1,275 orders every day. One every 68 seconds.

This is not a trivial administrative statistic. It raises a fundamental democratic question: who decides what citizens are allowed to see, discuss and criticise online?

🚨 THE NUMBERS DEMAND PUBLIC SCRUTINY

* Instagram received nearly 1 lakh orders.

* Facebook received around 80,000.

* YouTube received nearly 15,000.

* Meta's two platforms—Instagram and Facebook—accounted for roughly nine out of every ten orders directed to these three platforms.

For comparison, RTI information previously reported by The Indian Express showed 2,312 blocking orders sent through the Sahyog portal to 19 platforms between October 2024 and October 2025.

The scale of the subsequent increase deserves a detailed public explanation.

THE MOST DISTURBING QUESTION: CAN A MACHINE REMOVE OUR VOICE WITHOUT MEANINGFUL HUMAN REVIEW?

According to The Indian Express, Meta integrated its API with the government's Sahyog portal to comply with a shortened takedown deadline. The report says this enabled government-flagged content to be removed automatically, without a separate human review by the company.

Automation may make administration faster. But speed is not the same as justice.

What happens if an order is mistaken, overbroad or insufficiently justified? Who checks whether the content actually violates the law? How quickly can an ordinary citizen challenge the decision and restore lawful speech?

A system that can silence first and explain later needs exceptionally strong safeguards.

📢 WHY THIS MATTERS TO EVERY CITIZEN

The reported orders coincided with student protests against examination-paper leaks at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. The reporting also described takedowns affecting posts concerning the government's ethanol-blending policy and the West Bengal elections.

The presence of a takedown order does not, by itself, prove unlawful censorship. Governments have legitimate duties to address unlawful content, and the law permits restrictions in defined circumstances.

But criticism of the government, peaceful protest, investigative journalism and political disagreement must not be casually treated as threats merely because they are uncomfortable for those in power.

India's constitutional commitment to freedom of speech cannot survive on assurances alone. It requires lawful orders, transparent procedures, independent scrutiny and effective remedies.

⚖️ THE LAW MUST NOT BECOME A SHORTCUT AROUND DUE PROCESS

The reporting distinguishes the takedown mechanism associated with Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act from the separate blocking framework under Section 69A.

These are not interchangeable provisions. Their legal basis, procedures and safeguards matter. The public deserves clarity about which authority issued each order, what legal grounds were invoked and what opportunity affected users had to challenge it.

OUR DEMANDS

1. Publish regular, platform-wise statistics on government takedown orders, their legal grounds and their outcomes.
2. Ensure meaningful human and legal review of disputed or ambiguous directions.
3. Give affected users clear notice, subject to narrowly justified exceptions, and an effective appeal mechanism.
4. Disclose the safeguards governing automated integration between government portals and social-media platforms.
5. Ensure that peaceful dissent, journalism and legitimate political criticism are not suppressed through vague or overbroad directions.
6. Enable independent judicial scrutiny wherever legality or fundamental rights are contested.

India cannot call itself the world's largest democracy while treating transparency about restrictions on public speech as optional.

THE ISSUE IS NOT WHETHER GOVERNMENTS CAN ENFORCE THE LAW. THE ISSUE IS WHETHER THEY CAN DO SO WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY.

A democracy must protect citizens from unlawful content—but it must also protect citizens' right to question the state.

When posts disappear, citizens deserve to know why. When orders are issued, the public deserves to know under what authority. And when lawful speech is wrongly removed, there must be a meaningful remedy.

Digital India must not become a system in which technology makes silencing citizens easier than answering them.

SUPPORTING REPORTING

2. The Indian Express — Background on Sahyog and the growth of government-directed takedowns: https://t.co/vYXKHDlsAU

Two members of Congress have been quietly merging two separate site-blocking bills into one.

Representative Zoe Lofgren (D) of California and Senator Thom Tillis (R) of North Carolina's bill would let copyright holders petition federal courts to order American internet service providers and DNS resolvers to block entire foreign domains.

Comcast. Verizon. Spectrum. T-Mobile. Cloudflare. Google. OpenDNS. All of them, ordered to refuse to resolve a domain on the strength of a court order obtained by the MPA's lawyers.

Once the law exists, any foreign domain a federal judge finds objectionable disappears from the address book of every American household that does not run its own resolver.

This is what fourteen years of post-SOPA institutional memory loss looks like.

In 2012, the Stop Online Piracy Act died on the floor of Congress because the public found out what was in it before it passed. Wikipedia went dark in protest. Reddit went dark. Google put a black censor bar across its homepage. The bill sponsors retreated. The lesson the entertainment industry took from that defeat was not that the public opposed internet censorship. The lesson was that public attention was the problem.

So this time the bill has been drafted in private. There has been no blackout. There has been no consumer-facing campaign. The strategy is to negotiate the details quietly with the parties most able to refuse, and the public never finds out the law exists until they cannot reach a website.

In early 2026, the Supreme Court ruled in Cox Communications v. Sony Music that an ISP cannot be held liable for a billion dollars because some of its customers downloaded music. Justice Sotomayor, in a concurrence, complained that the ruling now permits ISPs to sell internet access to "every single infringer who wants one" without lifting a finger to prevent infringement. The publishers and the studios read that as a green light to ask Congress for the lever the courts no longer hand them.

This is the lever they want. A federal court order. A list of foreign domains. ISPs and DNS resolvers compelled by law to block on receipt.

The list of countries that already have laws like this includes the United Kingdom, France, Italy, Spain, Australia, India, Brazil, and Russia. The MPA cites this as evidence that the United States is behind. In Spain, IP-level blocking ordered by the football league has knocked legitimate businesses offline because they happened to share a server with a blocked domain. In Italy, the Piracy Shield system has blocked Cloudflare entirely on multiple occasions. In the United Kingdom, blocking orders have been used to take down sites that were not piracy sites at all, on the basis that they linked to piracy sites.

The collateral damage is the system working as designed. The blunter the instrument, the easier the enforcement.

There is no version of this law that targets only the bad actors. Domains are not isolated. Hosting is shared. CDNs are shared. The address book is a single document. Once the law exists, the list of blocked domains will only grow, the criteria will only loosen, and the appeal process will only formalize what was already done.

Anything that depends on resolving a foreign domain becomes contingent on the goodwill of a federal court and the lobbying budget of whoever wants the domain alive. Every shadow library, every IPTV mirror, every privacy-respecting service whose lawyers cannot match Disney's. All of them will be one petition away from disappearing from the address book of every household whose internet runs through Comcast.

Most people do not run a VPN, do not configure a custom DNS, do not know what an IP address is. Most people get the internet their ISP serves them. The bill is written for those people. The bill assumes that if the road is closed at the resolver, the destination effectively does not exist.

This bill will outlive its sponsors, its pretext, and the industries that bought it. Laws granting infrastructure-level censorship power do not get repealed. They get expanded. Every kill switch finds a hand.

When orders and reasons are secret by default, affected persons cannot test legality, necessity, proportionality, or factual errors except through protracted litigation. When in _Shreya Singhal v. Union of India_ (2015), the Supreme Court upheld Section 69A while relying on the existence of procedural safeguards and reasoned decisions, indicating that impacted users could approach court in writ remedies. However, due to the operational secrecy and providing copies of orders and notices those who are censored and prevented from obtaining judicial remedy.

The February 2026 amendments to the IT Rules, 2021 further increase these risks. The substituted Rule 3(1)(d) requires intermediaries to remove or disable access within three hours of receiving “actual knowledge”, which can arise from a court order or a written “reasoned intimation” by authorised government officers. While the rule lists what a “reasoned intimation” should contain, the legal basis, statutory provision, nature of the unlawful act, and specific URL/identifier, the three-hour window pressures platforms to comply promptly which may often occur without any substantive assessment. These inherently opaque censorship practices are being accelerated through "Sahyog" portal. Developed by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), the Sahyog portal operates entirely without statutory footing, only being anchored in the IT Rules, 2021 that are created by executive notification. It functions as a censorship clearinghouse that deliberately bypasses the established, albeit weak, procedural safeguards of Section 69A. By routing automated takedown directives directly to intermediaries under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, the portal structurally excludes citizens and impacted users from the grievance process.

We demand that the government introduce strictly judicially enforceable transparency requirements, publish all blocking orders, and restore the principles of natural justice to India's platform governance framework. Based on requests from our community we will also next week launch a rough public sheet in which social media users can input and add information on digital censorship.

Two members of Congress have been quietly merging two separate site-blocking bills into one.

Representative Zoe Lofgren (D) of California and Senator Thom Tillis (R) of North Carolina's bill would let copyright holders petition federal courts to order American internet service providers and DNS resolvers to block entire foreign domains.

Comcast. Verizon. Spectrum. T-Mobile. Cloudflare. Google. OpenDNS. All of them, ordered to refuse to resolve a domain on the strength of a court order obtained by the MPA's lawyers.

Once the law exists, any foreign domain a federal judge finds objectionable disappears from the address book of every American household that does not run its own resolver.

This is what fourteen years of post-SOPA institutional memory loss looks like.

In 2012, the Stop Online Piracy Act died on the floor of Congress because the public found out what was in it before it passed. Wikipedia went dark in protest. Reddit went dark. Google put a black censor bar across its homepage. The bill sponsors retreated. The lesson the entertainment industry took from that defeat was not that the public opposed internet censorship. The lesson was that public attention was the problem.

So this time the bill has been drafted in private. There has been no blackout. There has been no consumer-facing campaign. The strategy is to negotiate the details quietly with the parties most able to refuse, and the public never finds out the law exists until they cannot reach a website.

In early 2026, the Supreme Court ruled in Cox Communications v. Sony Music that an ISP cannot be held liable for a billion dollars because some of its customers downloaded music. Justice Sotomayor, in a concurrence, complained that the ruling now permits ISPs to sell internet access to "every single infringer who wants one" without lifting a finger to prevent infringement. The publishers and the studios read that as a green light to ask Congress for the lever the courts no longer hand them.

This is the lever they want. A federal court order. A list of foreign domains. ISPs and DNS resolvers compelled by law to block on receipt.

The list of countries that already have laws like this includes the United Kingdom, France, Italy, Spain, Australia, India, Brazil, and Russia. The MPA cites this as evidence that the United States is behind. In Spain, IP-level blocking ordered by the football league has knocked legitimate businesses offline because they happened to share a server with a blocked domain. In Italy, the Piracy Shield system has blocked Cloudflare entirely on multiple occasions. In the United Kingdom, blocking orders have been used to take down sites that were not piracy sites at all, on the basis that they linked to piracy sites.

The collateral damage is the system working as designed. The blunter the instrument, the easier the enforcement.

There is no version of this law that targets only the bad actors. Domains are not isolated. Hosting is shared. CDNs are shared. The address book is a single document. Once the law exists, the list of blocked domains will only grow, the criteria will only loosen, and the appeal process will only formalize what was already done.

Anything that depends on resolving a foreign domain becomes contingent on the goodwill of a federal court and the lobbying budget of whoever wants the domain alive. Every shadow library, every IPTV mirror, every privacy-respecting service whose lawyers cannot match Disney's. All of them will be one petition away from disappearing from the address book of every household whose internet runs through Comcast.

Most people do not run a VPN, do not configure a custom DNS, do not know what an IP address is. Most people get the internet their ISP serves them. The bill is written for those people. The bill assumes that if the road is closed at the resolver, the destination effectively does not exist.

This bill will outlive its sponsors, its pretext, and the industries that bought it. Laws granting infrastructure-level censorship power do not get repealed. They get expanded. Every kill switch finds a hand.

Statement: IFF condemns the internet shutdown in Connaught Place ahead of today's protest. We are tracing the suspension order.

New Delhi, 2 October 2026

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) condemns the suspension of mobile internet services in and around Connaught Place, New Delhi, this morning. At 9:40 am, Jio subscribers in the area received a message stating: "As per government instructions Internet services have been stopped in your area till further notice." The shutdown took effect before a protest called for 11 am at Jantar Mantar, seeking the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, had even begun. 

Delhi Police has refused permission for the gathering, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 are in force across New Delhi district, and entry and exit at eleven metro stations have been closed. On Gandhi Jayanti, the answer to a call for protest in the capital has been to switch off the internet for everyone who lives, works, trades and reports in its centre. We call for the immediate restoration of services. 

At the time of release of this statement, we have not been able to locate any suspension order published by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Department of Telecommunications, the Government of NCT of Delhi or the Delhi Police. The public does not know who directed this shutdown, on what grounds, over what area, or until when. IFF is attempting to trace the order and will make it public as soon as we obtain a copy.

In Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, (2020) 3 SCC 637, the Supreme Court held that speech and trade over the internet are protected under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution, and that every suspension order must be published, reasoned, proportionate and limited in time. Under Section 20(2)(b) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024, only the Union or State Home Secretary may issue such an order, for reasons recorded in writing. The order must be published and must specify the area, the services and a fixed duration and it may be passed only where no other reasonable means would serve. A shutdown announced to subscribers as lasting "till further notice", imposed before a single person had assembled, cannot be squared with these safeguards. It follows repeated suspensions around Jantar Mantar in July 2026. Switching off the network is becoming a routine response to protest in the national capital. IFF condemns the internet shutdown in parts of Central Delhi. 

We call upon the Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi to:

1. Immediately restore mobile internet services in Connaught Place and all affected parts of Central Delhi.

2. Publish the suspension order forthwith, together with the reasons recorded in writing.

3. Disclose the issuing authority, the precise areas and services covered, and the period of operation.

4. Place the order before the Review Committee within five days, as the Rules require, and make its findings public.

Statement : IFF condemns the internet shutdown in parts of Central Delhi. No suspension order has been made public.

New Delhi, 20 July 2026

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) condemns the suspension of mobile internet services imposed today, 20 July 2026, in parts of Central Delhi, including the area around Jantar Mantar. The shutdown coincided with the 'Chalo Sansad' march called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on the opening day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament, where thousands of students and young people had gathered to press their demands. Permission for the march was refused. Prohibitory orders were imposed under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Routes to Parliament were sealed, and metro stations including, Patel Chowk, Rajiv Chowk and Janpath were closed. Amid reports of the use of force to disperse protesters, mobile internet was then switched off, reportedly "as a precautionary measure". We urge the immediate restoration of all telecommunication services in the capital and an end to internet shutdowns across India.

The developments of today are of immense consequence to the future of our democracy. The voices gathered at Jantar Mantar, and the residents of the national capital, need to be heard the loudest, not silenced en masse.

No order has been made public

At the time of release of this statement, no copy of any suspension order has been published by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Department of Telecommunications, the Government of NCT of Delhi or the Delhi Police. Residents of the capital do not know which authority directed the shutdown, on what grounds, over which precise areas, for which services, or for what duration. An unpublished order is an unaccountable order. It cannot be challenged before a court, and the judicial review guaranteed by the Supreme Court becomes illusory. Some reports further indicate the deployment of network jammers in parts of Central Delhi, including near Jantar Mantar. Jamming equipment finds no sanction in the legal framework for the suspension of telecommunication services at all. If jammers were deployed, the government must disclose under what legal authority.

Binding safeguards violated

On 10 January 2020, the Supreme Court in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India, (2020) 3 SCC 637 held that the freedom of speech and expression, and the freedom to carry on trade or business through the medium of the internet, are protected under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution. The Court directed that every order suspending telecom services must be published. Reasons must be recorded in writing. The restriction must be proportionate, adopting the least restrictive measure available. It cannot continue indefinitely. It is subject to judicial review, and to scrutiny by a review committee.

Parliament has since replaced the framework of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885. Under Section 20(2)(b) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023, telecommunication services may be suspended only on the occurrence of a public emergency or in the interest of public safety, on the grounds specified in that provision, and for reasons recorded in writing. The Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024, notified on 22 November 2024, give effect to this power. A suspension order may be issued only by the Union Home Secretary or the State Home Secretary. An officer not below the rank of Joint Secretary may act in unavoidable circumstances, subject to confirmation by the competent authority within twenty four hours. Every order must clearly define the geographical area and the specific services suspended, and cannot remain in operation beyond fifteen days. Every order must also be published. A Review Committee must meet within five days of the order and record its findings on whether it complies with Section 20(2).

These safeguards are not being followed

If we account for today's shutdown against this legal architecture. The order is unpublished, in breach of Anuradha Bhasin and the Suspension Rules, 2024 alike. No recorded reasons are available to the public despite little to no reports of violence and consistent calls for the protest to be peaceful by the CJP and other organisers. The precise areas and services covered are undisclosed and so is the duration. Whether the competent authority even issued the order cannot be known. Whether the Review Committee will examine it cannot be verified. While the Suspension Rules prescribe no outer time limit for publication, a gap we have previously flagged, it cannot cut against the spirit of the Anuradha Bhasin judgement. A blanket suspension across densely populated parts of the capital, imposed as a "precaution" against a march to Parliament, is the opposite of a narrowly tailored, least restrictive measure. A shutdown timed to a protest restricts the freedoms of speech and assembly at the very moment they matter most.

The human cost of a shutdown

Access to the internet is a digital right on which the exercise of our fundamental freedoms now depends. When the network goes dark in Central Delhi, a journalist at Jantar Mantar cannot file her report or broadcast live. A street vendor on the surrounding roads cannot accept a UPI payment. A gig worker loses a day's earnings. A parent cannot confirm that a child who joined the march is safe. Cutting off communications prevents people from reaching out for help and manufactures panic in a moment which demands calm. These costs fall hardest on daily wage earners and small traders who can least absorb them. Internet based communications also promote trust between people and their government. 

A pattern, not an aberration

Delhi has seen this before. On 19 December 2019, mobile services were suspended for the first time in the capital's history during the protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, in areas including Seelampur, Jamia Nagar and Mandi House. On 26 January 2021, the Ministry of Home Affairs suspended internet services in Singhu, Ghazipur, Tikri, Mukarba Chowk, Nangloi and their adjoining areas during the farmers' protests. According to the #KeepItOn coalition's report released in March 2026, India recorded 65 internet shutdowns in 2025, the highest of any democracy in the world, and accounts for 920 of the 2,102 shutdowns documented globally since 2016. We have consistently advocated against the harm these disruptions cause, from Jammu and Kashmir to Rajasthan, and from Haryana to Manipur, where a shutdown in 2023 ran for over two hundred days. The orders are rarely published on time, and the findings of review committees never see daylight.

Our demands

We call upon the Government of India and the Government of NCT of Delhi to:

1. Immediately restore all suspended telecommunication and internet services in Central Delhi.
2. Publish forthwith every suspension order passed on or around 20 July 2026, together with the reasons recorded in writing, as mandated by Anuradha Bhasin and the Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024.
3. Disclose the issuing authority, the grounds, the precise areas and services covered, and the period of operation, and clarify whether network jammers were deployed and under what legal authority.
4. Place the order before the Review Committee within five days as required by the Rules, and make its findings public.
5. Reform Section 20(2)(b) of the Telecommunications Act, 2023 to provide for independent prior authorisation and real consequences for unlawful suspensions.

IFF will file applications under the Right to Information Act, 2005 seeking copies of the suspension orders and the records of the Review Committee, and is examining further legal remedies.

text:
Ireland is prosecuting a man for his signs — I'm going back for his trial 🇮🇪

Hugh Fagan sits on a bench in Wexford with seven homemade signs and his headphones on. The Irish state has charged him with a public order offence. His trial is October 27, and Rebel News has hired him a lawyer.

The Irish government is prosecuting a man for his signs.

His name is Hugh Fagan. He lives in Wexford, a lovely little tourist town in the south-east of Ireland — cobbled streets, coffee shops, a medieval abbey. Most days he walks down to the town square, four blocks from his house, and sits on a bench with seven handmade signs propped up around him.

He wears headphones. He doesn’t shout. He doesn’t hand out leaflets or ask anyone for anything. He isn’t a member of any party. If you want to talk to him, he takes the headphones off and talks to you — and he told me that happens every day. If you don’t, he just sits there.

And for that, a summons came in the post. He’s charged with a public order offence. When I asked him which of the seven signs he was being charged over, he said the police hadn’t told him, that he’d find out in court.

I (@EzraLevant) sat with Hugh in the square this spring, when I was in Ireland for Kirk Loco’s case, and talked to him for 20 minutes.

(It was filmed in May, so when Hugh says his hearing is “next week,” that was an earlier appearance. His trial is now set for Tuesday, October 27.)

Let me tell you how he started.

In May of last year, he was walking past a church near the Tesco on a Sunday. A funeral was coming out, the casket was being put into the hearse, and a beggar was lying across the entrance. Hugh said to himself, enough is enough, and the next week he was in the square with two signs; now, there are seven.

They’re about mass immigration, about churches being burned down across Europe, about the safety of women and children, about the European Union.

I’ll be honest with you: the signs are blunt. I read one of them out loud on camera, and I don’t agree with every word. Where I disagree, it’s with the style more than the substance — I’m worried about mass immigration too, and about what’s happening to women in Ireland. But even if I disagreed with all of it, that’s the point of freedom of speech. It’s the gift you give your opponents if you want it for yourself.

Here’s what gets me.

The Guards — that’s what the Irish call their police — get called on Hugh almost every week. People walk up to him and scream “racist” and “fascist” in his face. The buskers have told him to move. Pro-Palestine activists have told him “nobody wants you here.” Tourists have stood over him waiting for the Guards to come and arrest him. The local paper has written about him twice.

None of those people have been charged with anything. The only person charged is the man sitting quietly on the bench.

Hugh said something to me that stuck. “We’re living in the upside down at the moment,” he said. “What’s true is not true anymore.”

By the way, Hugh told me he’s lived in four countries and never so much as had a parking ticket. He’s not a troublemaker. He’s an unusual man with an unusual way of making his point — I called him the Unreasonable Man, after Bernard Shaw’s line that all progress depends on the unreasonable man, and he liked that.

It reminded me of my friend Chris Elston back in Canada — better known as @BillboardChris — who stands on street corners with a sandwich board. Eccentric, maybe. Criminal? Come on.

This is the pattern in Ireland now, and the more I look at it the more worried I get. Kirk Loco was charged under an anti-terror law for a tweet — for reposting a warning that a migrant had exposed himself to a teenaged girl on a bus. The migrant wasn’t charged; Kirk was. His next hearing is in Bray on October 23, four days before Hugh’s. And now a man with cardboard signs.

The Taoiseach, Ireland's prime minister, goes abroad and calls the country a bastion of free speech. The Irish media cheer the prosecutions on. Nobody in Ireland is pushing back in an organized way.

So we are.

An old friend of mine used to say it’s easier to fight in the first ditch than in the last ditch. Hugh Fagan is the first ditch. If the state can shut up a quiet man with signs in a tourist town, it can shut up anyone. He’s the tripwire. If they get him, they move on to the next one, and the next.

We’ve hired him a proper legal team: Laoise de Brún, a Dublin barrister, and Padraig Langsch, a solicitor. They’re the same lawyers defending Kirk. Their fee for Hugh’s case is €10,000 euros, all in. We’ve already paid half, through the Irish free speech crowdfund you’ve been supporting. The rest is due after the hearing.

And I’ll be in Wexford District Court on October 27, in person, live-tweeting from inside and filming outside. I’ll be in Bray for Kirk four days earlier. One trip, two trials, and you’ll get a report from both courtrooms.

ట్రాన్స్ జెండర్స్ ను ట్రాఫిక్ అసిస్టెంట్లుగా...
నియమించి వారి ఆత్మగౌరవాన్ని పెంచాం 

పోలీస్ అమరవీరుల సంస్మరణ దినం కార్యక్రమంలో ముఖ్యమంత్రి రేవంత్ రెడ్డి గారు…

ఈ రోజు మనందరికీ ఎంతో భావోద్వేగమైన రోజు.. పోలీస్ అమరులను స్మరించుకునే రోజు 

సమాజం కోసం ప్రాణాలను త్యాగం చేసిన పోలీస్ అమరులకు నివాళులు 

దేశవ్యాప్తంగా దేవ్ సింగ్, ప్రమోద్ కుమార్, గాజుల సౌమ్య విధి నిర్వహణలో మరణించారు 

శాంతిభద్రతల పరిరక్షణలో వారి త్యాగాలను మరువలేం 

అమరుల కుటుంబం ఒంటరి కాదు.. వారి కుటుంబాలకు ప్రభుత్వం అండగా ఉంటుంది 

రాష్ట్ర అభివృద్ధి శాంతి భద్రతల పరిరక్షణ ఎంతో ముఖ్యం 

అందుకే పోలీస్ శాఖకు మా ప్రభుత్వం అత్యంత ప్రాధాన్యం ఇస్తున్నాం 

పోలీస్ శాఖలో మరో 5 వేల ఉద్యోగాల భర్తీకి చర్యలు తీసుకున్నాం 

2028 లోగా పోలీస్ శాఖలో అన్ని ఖాళీలను భర్తీ చేస్తాం 

గతంలో ఎన్నడూ లేని విధంగా 112 డీఎస్పీలను నియమించాం 

ట్రాన్స్ జెండర్స్ ను ట్రాఫిక్ అసిస్టెంట్లుగా నియమించి వారి ఆత్మగౌరవాన్ని పెంచాం 

గతంలో విధి నిర్వహణలో వీరమరణం పొందిన కానిస్టేబుళ్ల కు రూ. 40 లక్షలు ఎక్స్గ్రేషియా ఉంటే దానిని ఏకంగా  ₹ 1 కోటి  పెంచాం.
 
హెడ్‌ కానిస్టేబుళ్ళు, ఏఎస్‌ఐ లకు గతంలో రూ.45 లక్షలుగా ఉన్న పరిహారాన్ని రూ.కోటికి పెంచాం.  

ఎస్‌ఐల కు 45 లక్షలు, ఇన్‌స్పెక్టర్లకు 50 లక్షలు ఉంటే దీనిని రూ.1.25 కోట్లు కు పెంచారు. 

డీఎస్పీ, అడిషనల్‌ ఎస్పీ స్థాయి అధికారులకు 50 లక్షలు ఉంటే మేం రూ.1.50 కోట్లు పెంచాము

ఎస్పీ, ఐపీఎస్‌ అధికారులకు కోటి రూపాయలు పరిహారం ఉంటే  దానిని రూ.2 కోట్ల కు  పెంచాము.

ఇది కేవలం ఆర్ధిక సహాయం కాదు.. పోలీసు అమరవీరుల కుటుంబాలకు ప్రభుత్వం ఇచ్చే గౌరవం 

యంగ్ ఇండియా పోలీస్ స్కూల్ ను ప్రారంభించి హోమ్ గార్డు నుంచి డీజీపీ స్థాయి వరకు వారి పిల్లలకు ఇందులో అవకాశం కల్పించాం 

విధి నిర్వహణలో ప్రాణాలు కోల్పోయే హోంగార్డుల కుటుంబాలకు రూ.5 లక్షలు ఎక్స్‌గ్రేషియా అందిస్తున్నాం . 

ఈ ఎక్స్‌గ్రేషియాను రూ.10 లక్షలకు పెంచాలని డీజీపీని ఆదేశిస్తున్నా 

కాలంతో పాటు నేర స్వభావం మారుతోంది 

కొత్త సవాళ్లను ఎదుర్కొనేందుకు పోలీస్ శాఖను ఆధునీకరించాలని నిర్ణయించాం 

ఆధునిక సాంకేతికతను వినియోగించాలని నిర్ణయం తీసుకున్నాం 

సాంకేతికత ఎంత పెరిగినా పోలీసులు మానవీయ దృక్పథం మారకూడదు 

డ్రగ్స్, గంజాయి వ్యాప్తి అత్యంత ప్రమాదకరం 

యువత మాదకద్రవ్యాల బారిన పడకుండా చూడాలీ 

డ్రగ్స్ నియంత్రణలో ఈగల్ ఫోర్స్ పనితీరును, డీజీపీ ని అభినందిస్తున్నా 

కల్తీ ఆహారంపై ఉక్కు పాదంతో అణచివేసేందుకు టీజీ సేఫ్ ను తీసుకొచ్చాం 

షీ టీమ్స్ సేవలను కొనసాగిస్తూ మహిళల భద్రతను మరింత బలోపేతం చేస్తున్నాం. 

మహిళలకు అండగా నిలిచే సామాజిక బాధ్యతను పెంచడానికి స్టాండ్ విత్ హర్ కార్యక్రమాన్ని ఈ ఏడాది మార్చిలో ప్రారంభించాం. 

మహిళలు, పిల్లలకు అత్యవసర పరిస్థితుల్లో తక్షణ రక్షణ అందించడానికి ఏప్రిల్‌లో స్పందన – తక్షణ రక్షణ బృందాలను ప్రారంభించాం.
 
మహిళలు, చిన్నారులకు సంబంధించిన కేసుల్లో పోలీసులు మరింత సున్నితంగా వ్యవహరించాలి. 

బాధితులకు న్యాయం అందించడంలో జాప్యం జరగకూడదు. 

మహిళల భద్రత కేవలం పోలీసు శాఖ బాధ్యత కాదు. సమాజంలోని ప్రతి ఒక్కరూ తమ బాధ్యతగా భావించాలి.

చివరిగా పోలీసు అమరవీరుల కుటుంబ సభ్యులతో ప్రత్యేకంగా ఒక మాట చెప్పాలనుకుంటున్నా. 

మీరు కోల్పోయిన వ్యక్తిని ఎవరూ తిరిగి తీసుకురాలేరు. 

మీ కుటుంబాల్లో ఏర్పడిన లోటును ఎవరూ పూర్తిగా భర్తీ చేయలేరు. 

కానీ మీ బాధలో మీరు ఒంటరివారు కాదు.. మీకు తెలంగాణ ప్రభుత్వం అండగా ఉంటుంది. పోలీసు శాఖ అండగా ఉంటుంది. తెలంగాణ సమాజం అండగా ఉంటుంది. 

ఈ రోజు పోలీసు శాఖలో పనిచేస్తున్న ప్రతి అధికారి, ప్రతి సిబ్బందికి ఒక మాట చెప్పాలనుకుంటున్నా. 

మీ క్రమశిక్షణే మీ బలం. మీ నిజాయితీయే మీ గౌరవం. ప్రజలకు మీరు అందించే భరోసాయే మీకు లభించే గొప్ప గుర్తింపు. 

ప్రజల భద్రతకు మీరు అండగా నిలవండి. మీ సంక్షేమానికి, మీ కుటుంబాల భవిష్యత్తుకు ఈ ప్రభుత్వం అండగా ఉంటుంది. 

అమరుల త్యాగాలను గౌరవిద్దాం. వారి ఆశయాలను కొనసాగిద్దాం. శాంతియుతమైన, సురక్షితమైన, అభివృద్ధి చెందిన తెలంగాణను నిర్మించుకుందాం.

CM Revanth Reddy announces all vacant posts in the Police department will be filled by 2028

CM declares increase of ex-gratia for  Home Guards to Rs 10 lakhs from Rs 5 lakhs 

Recruitment of 110 DSP posts is unprecedented in Telangana history 

Calls upon  police to handle cases involving women and children with greater sensitivity. 

Avoid delay in delivering justice 

CM orders police to protect youth from being addicted to drugs 

TG Government accorded top priority to the maintenance of the law and order 

CM Revanth Reddy participates in the Police Commemoration Parade at Police Martyrs Memorial , Goshamahal Police stadium in Hyderabad today.

Hyderabad: 

Honourable Chief Minister Shri A Revanth Reddy has announced that all the vacant posts in the Telangana Police department would be filled by 2028. In a major decision,  the Chief Minister declared that the ex-gratia amount would be increased to Rs 10 lakhs from Rs 5 lakhs for Home Guards in the service. 

Addressing a gathering at the Police Commemoration Parade in Hyderabad today, the CM instructed DGP CV Anand to take necessary measures towards increasing the ex-gratia to Home Guards to Rs 10 lakhs, who lost their lives while performing their duties. 

Stating that the government has already 
issued notification to fill  5,000 vacancies in the Police department, the CM said that the government is committed to fill all vacancies in the police wing by 2028. 

CM Revanth Reddy noted that the recruitment of 112 DSPs posts is  unprecedented in the history of Telangana state. Alongside, we were also appointing transgenders as traffic assistants and enhanced their self-respect and dignity in the society. 

Calling upon the police to deal with the cases involving women and children with greater sensitivity, the Chief Minister emphasized that there should be no delay in delivering justice to the victims.
Ensuring the safety of women is not solely the responsibility of the police department. Every individual in society should also take the responsibility of women's safety.

The CM worried about the drug menace  and appealed to the police to ensure that the youth should not fall victim to the drug abuse. CM Revanth Reddy commended the 'Eagle Force' for their unstinted efforts in  curbing drug trafficking and also appreciated the DGP's endeavour. 

Since the maintenance of law and order is crucial for the development of the state, the Chief Minister said that the government is giving top priority to strengthen the police department.

CM Revanth Reddy highlighted the initiatives taken to strengthen the police wing. We were leveraging modern technology in the police department to effectively address new challenges. Besides, the human-centric approach of the police force must remain unchanged, the Chief Minister said that 'TG SAFE' was established to take a firm and  uncompromising stance against food adulteration.SHE teams were formed for women safety and also launched the 'Stand With Her' initiative to foster a greater sense of social responsibility in supporting women. 'Spandana'—a set of 'Immediate Protection Teams'— was another initiative enforced to provide instant safeguarding for women and children during emergencies.

The  'Young India Police School' was established to provide educational opportunities for the children of police personnel from Home Guards to the rank of DGP.

The Chief Minister listed out the welfare measures for the police.  The ex-gratia amount has been increased to Rs 1 crore from Rs 45 lakhs for Head Constables and ASIs,  For Sub-Inspectors, the amount has been increased from ₹45 lakh to ₹1.25 crore, and for Inspectors, from ₹50 lakh to ₹1.25 crore. It was Rs 1.50 crore for officers at the rank of DSP and Additional SP. The  compensation for SP and IPS officers was enhanced to Ra 2 crore from Rs One Crore. " The    increased compensation is not merely financial assistance. It is a gesture of respect from the government toward the families of police martyrs" 

Remembering the Police Martyrs who laid down their lives in their duties, the Chief Minister said that the discipline is police strength and the  integrity is their honour. The sense of security police provide to the public is the greatest recognition to the cops. Police are not alone in their grief. The state Government stands with the bereaved family and the entire society of Telangana also stands with you". 

The CM asserted that police should continue to stand as a pillar of safety for the people as this government remains committed to their welfare and the future of families. " Let us honour the sacrifices of our martyrs and carry forward their vision. Together, let us build a peaceful, secure, and prosperous Telangana." 

Paying tributes to the police personnel who sacrificed their lives for the sake of society, CM Revanth Reddy recalled that the martyrs Cops - Dev Singh, Pramod Kumar, and Gajula Soumya who laid down their lives while in thier duty.Their sacrifices in maintaining law and order can never be forgotten.

Then come Japa (the chantong of a sacred mantra), Tapa (a disciplined spiritual practice or austerity), Yoga, and then medicine.Even this transformation through medicine has been acknowledged by Rishi Patanjali. I am not saying this; Rishi Patanjali is saying this.
Now, in the Vibhuti Pada (the third chapter of Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras) there are descriptions of various siddhis, or extraordinary attainments, do you understand?
Among them is one Siddhi called Pratibha Jnana (a special or intuitive form of knowledge).
In the Vibhuti Pada, in Sutras 33 and 36, the Rishi refers to this knowledge as Pratibha Jnana.
When Pratibha Jnana is attained, the practitioner sees and hears the unlimited past and future. He experiences divine touch, divine fragrance, and divine taste. A transformation takes place within the person, you understand.
There is a transformation of the human being.
So, there are two methods here: Naam Jap, the chanting of the Divine Name, and meditation.
Now, where should you meditate?
Our Yoga says: “Whatever exists in the universe (Macrocosm) exists within the individual being (Microcosm), and whatever exists within the individual being (Microcosm) exists in the universe (Macrocosm).”
If the entire universe (Macrocosm) exists within you, then whatever you seek, you will find within yourself. You will not find it outside.
Even the Creator of the universe is within you.
In Bikaner, a head of a cancer department came to meet me. I asked him, “Why is cancer not cured?”
He said, “Genes are formed which give an order to the body’s tissues to commit suicide; they induce them to do so. And, obeying that command, the tissues begin to die, the body deteriorates, and the person dies. This is absolutely a fact, but what that force is—we have not been able to trace it.”
They give chemotherapy, and through it, both RBCs and WBCs are destroyed, and then blood is transfused. In this way, after developing cancer, a person dies within six years.
Then, after developing AIDS, a person will die in seven or eight years. The plans that this government is making are wrong. I am saying that, to this day, not a single person who has been HIV-positive has become HIV-negative anywhere in the world, understand?
And no matter how much money you spend on this, what difference will it make? In Odisha, there are the highest number of AIDS and cancer patients, and they have started giving a pension of only two hundred rupees per month to AIDS patients. What will that achieve? The medicines for an AIDS patient cost at least ten to fifteen thousand rupees per month.
So, Dharana (fixed concentration), Dhyana (meditation), and Samadhi (deep absorption) are the subtler limbs. As soon as the Kundalini is awakened, the first five koshas(sheaths) will become activated —Annamaya (matter), Pranamaya (life force), Manomaya (mind), and Vijnanamaya (knowledge),understand?
In this way, the awakened Kundalini takes control of the practitioner’s body, prana, mind, and intellect, and makes the yogic movements happen by themselves.
What is happening today is that a yoga teacher stands outside and makes people practice yoga. I am not talking about that. I am saying that the doctor within you (inner consciousness) knows much better which organ of your body is not functioning properly; the doctor outside does not know as much.
But it is going on, all right; it is also being sold—there is nothing wrong with that.
And the unfortunate thing is that, in this country, religion is being sold. In the West, it is sold anyway; now it is being sold here too.
So I said to that doctor, the Head of the Cancer Department, “Doctor Sahib, the matter is like this: if, in a person, Ravana has become dominant and has started doing his work, but Rama is also within him, isn’t he? The Divine is also within him.
If, in a person in whom the demon has become dominant, the Divine becomes dominant—by some method—then, because the one who protects is greater than the one who kills, he will say, ‘Do not obey the demon.’ So what will happen?”
Then he said, “Yes, then cancer should be cured.”
From that time, I started saying in Rajasthan: there is a war between the Divine and the demon within us. In this way, you can destroy the demon. The victory of the Divine is possible.
Since then, this work has begun. I do not know how many lakhs of people have been cured of cancer and AIDS.
Cancer is a matter related to samskaras from previous births. AIDS is the sin of this birth. AIDS is never obtained for free.
People make a lot of excuses in front of me.
This method is so simple that it can bring about a cure just through my photograph. Now, the results that my photograph is producing have made the West very astonished.
It does not go even one second before or after the time requested for meditation; then the meditation comes to an end. So, for science, this has become a very profound challenge—that matter is benefiting the spirit. This benefit is not happening without reason.
I, too, had to undertake spiritual practices. Let me tell you: the transformation that has taken place within me—only then can I bring about this transformation in you. Otherwise, I https://t.co/DjX0km9V2p you understand?
Now I was surrounded by difficulties. So people told me, “You are going through the Markesh period.”
I did not know what Markesh was. They explained it to me, and I said, ‘It comes to everyone. It will come to me too. What is the problem?’ Then they said, “You can also be saved from it.”
I asked, “How?”
They said, “Chant the Mahamrityunjaya Mantra.” It was a very strange ritualistic practice, that whole thing.
I said, “I cannot do it by myself anyway. Let this Markesh come.”
Then they said, “Yes, it can also be done through Gayatri Japa.”
At that time, when I started, I did not even know what Gayatri meant.
Later, when the consciousness arose within me, people said, “You have attained Siddhi”
I did not know what Siddhi was or what it meant. Then they said, “You have reached the finishing point. Use this for tantric purposes; people will give you lakhs of rupees.”
I thought, “Why should I give gold and take iron? That would be foolishness.”
If God has brought about this transformation, then I will use it in my life for the welfare of humanity, not for money.
So, until today, God has preserved my honour. Understand?
Now that I understood. So, what actually happened? The one hundred and twenty-five thousand Japa of the Gayatri Mantra has been completed.’ Now I understand that completing one hundred and twenty-five thousand Japa of the Gayatri Mantra itself has no significance. The result came from that concentration. The five-faced picture of Vedmata Gayatri was in front of me, and on one side, death was standing. During the Japa, I continuously prayed before that picture: ‘Somehow, save my life. That concentration transformed this body.
Where did the organs go? But whatever is seen is seen through the eyes. What is this light within? I concentrated on that light. Then what did I hear? A humming sound, like a bee, was coming from inside the abdomen.
I said, ‘The voice comes from the throat. How can there be a humming sound like a bee in the abdomen?
I concentrated on the sound, and the Gayatri Mantra was being chanted. It was being chanted from the navel. I had chanted it from the throat, but it was being chanted from the navel.
It was like a bicycle chain that keeps moving endlessly. The chanting continued without end. I was greatly astonished.
Now, when this body was transformed. There is an energy behind the human body. Not even a single hair is without energy.
The Vedas have called it Agni (Fire). It is present everywhere.
The moment I stepped back, my body was transformed into that energy. This body was transformed into a divine form.
It happened in an innocent way. I never wanted to become what I am today. Nature pushed me into it, and I have simply kept moving forward.
Then the writings of Swami Vivekananda Ji came into the picture. He said that this path cannot be followed without a Guru. So I accepted Nath Ji [Mahāyogī Baba Shri Gangai Nath Ji Maharaj (Brahmaleen)] as my Guru.
My Gurudev’s ashram is 27 kilometers from Bikaner, on the way towards Punjab, at Jamsar. There is a railway station and a bus stand there, and the ashram is still there today.
So I accepted him as my Guru. I did not know what a Guru gives or takes. I thought, ‘Well, he has renounced worldly life, so we householders are the ones who provide him with food and clothing. What does he have to give us?’
At the time of his passing, he said to me, ‘You have to carry out the work ahead.
I was working for the Railways as a Head Clerk, understand? I retired seven years early, on my Guru’s command. The Guru’s command is a very strict principle. If you do not follow the Guru’s command, your spiritual progress can be obstructed.
So I took premature retirement, seven years early, and I have been doing this work ever since. Do you understand it or not? I’ll put it plainly: earlier, I worked for the Railways; now, I work for Gangai Nath Ji. In the Railway job, there was a fixed retirement age; in this job, there is no retirement at all.
For different illnesses, the Kundalini works on the particular system that has become irregular. It stimulates and tones it up, and continues to work on it until it becomes properly fit and healthy. Do you understand it or not? In this way, Yogic movements will happen; it will not happen without your willingness. When you sit down for meditation, look at me here (at the Ajna Chakra), offer your salutations and prayers, and then begin your meditation. In prayer, ask for the duration you wish to meditate, and the Yoga will begin. Keep a clock in front of you. The meditation will not go even one second before or after the time you have requested. An American woman told her husband, ‘Please sit in the other room. I’ll sit here and meditate.’ She began her meditation and told him that she had started. She asked him to come and wake her at the appointed time. Her husband was two or three seconds late, but her eyes opened exactly on time. She said, ‘What did you do?’ He replied, ‘It’s only been two seconds. It is that precise—the clock within is working. And there, Yoga is being practiced simply through the photograph.
I stayed in America for a month, understand? So I said, ‘You should not be so proud of your science. According to the Rig Veda, the three koshas (sheaths) must first become conscious.’
The transformation that takes place in human beings is not specific to any particular caste or any particular country. Kundalini exists in every human being, indeed in every living being. And this is about Self-realization, brother. There is no question of proving or disproving anything here. If I give you something and you choose not to accept it, the argument can simply go on and on. I am not giving you anything.
I learned to read the book that is this body. My Guru taught me how to read it, and that is what I am teaching you—to keep reading until you have read its very last letter.
Now, the scientists are puzzled.
I am 81 years old—I am talking about the government here. They say, ‘He is an 81-year-old man; he will die in a year or two.’ I said, ‘I too have to die, and so do you. But my photograph will not die. My photograph will remain as long as this world exists.’ This evolution will continue, and humanity will attain perfection. Do you understand it or not?
“Maharshi Aurobindo has said that this body will be transformed into a divine form, and that the human race of the future will attain divine bodies. So, if that transformation has happened in me, why should it not happen in all of you?
“Then I chanted Krishna’s mantra. I said, ‘What is this? Then I chanted Krishna’s mantra and thought, ‘What is this? There is so much power in mantras!’ Do you understand it or not?’ I attained Siddhi of Krishna too.
Both these Siddhis—Nirguna-Nirakara and Saguna-Sakara—have been attained by me in a single lifetime. Look, Aurobindo has spoken very clearly about this.
Aurobindo said that in this country there are two ways of spiritual practice. There are those who worship the Divine in His Saguna-Sakara form—the manifest, personal form—and as a result, a chemical change takes place in their bodies.
Then there are those who receive initiation from a renunciate and practice complete mantra japa of the Nirguna-Nirakara—the formless, attributeless Divine. A chemical change takes place in them as well. But when they die, the chemical changes that have taken place in the body do not carry over into the next birth. We believe in the principle of rebirth; those changes do not pass into the body of the next life.
Aurobindo therefore said that if the Siddhis of both Saguna and Nirguna were attained in the same person, in the same body, with all the changes taking place within a single lifetime rather than being carried over into another birth, then the welfare of all humanity would be achieved.
That has happened in me—in an innocent way. Do you understand it or not? I never wanted this to happen, nor had I ever imagined that such a thing was possible. But now, there is no other path for me to follow except this one. So, brother, I have already lived 81 years—who knows whether I will live another year or two. Do good and forget about it.
Baba Gangai Nath [Mahāyogī Baba Shri Gangai Nath Ji Maharaj (Brahmaleen)] sponsors this. Do you understand it or not? I never believed in the idea of a sponsor. I never did. But now, you see - the Nine Nathas are immortal. This is according to the Kashmir Shaivism tradition, Do you understand it or not?
Nowadays, the moment people hear the name Kashmir, they start talking about the conflict between Hindus and Muslims. But according to Kashmir Shaivism, God performs five functions: Śrishti (creation), Sthiti (preservation), Laya (dissolution), Tirodhāna (concealment), and Anugraha (grace). And Anugraha—the fifth function—is the work of the Guru.
When you become intoxicated with the Divine Name, all other forms of intoxication will disappear, do you understand it or not? Meditation will happen effortlessly. So, do not give up chanting the Name. I am not saying this; the sage Patanjali is saying it, do you understand it or not? When Prātibha Jñāna is attained, Siddhis arise, understand?
In this way, when you are able to see into the future, you will see everything—birth, death, attack, retaliation. Your material science works on the principle that whatever word has been spoken remains in the universe and can be heard. Our Yogic philosophy says that if there is a word, there must have been someone who spoke it; therefore, it is possible to see and hear that person speaking it.
Buddha, for instance, knew about his previous three or four hundred births. But no one knows what will happen tomorrow.
The situation is the same in all the religions of the world. They all say, ‘Look back, look back—see what Rama did, what Krishna did, what Buddha did, what Mahavira did, what Muhammad did, what Jesus did, what so-and-so did.’ They keep looking backward while moving forward. If you keep looking backward while moving forward, won't you stumble? Won't you fall into a pit?
Only our Yogic philosophy says that the unlimited future can be seen and heard.
In this way, when you are in a state of meditation, you may see the deaths of many people you know. You may see approximately at what age they will die and what the cause of death will be—and just as you saw it, they will die. One after another, ten, twenty, thirty people may die. And if, by chance, the thought comes to you, ‘Are you going to live forever?’ then you will see how you will die.
A person is very afraid of death. So when you see yourself dying, you become frightened, and then you remember God again. When death comes, God is remembered—‘Save me somehow!’ Then, closing your eyes, you pray, ‘O God, they say You are compassionate. I was unworthy; I have committed all these sins. Please forgive me this time. I will never do it again!’
And then, just as Arjuna saw only the bird's eye, you will have no desire for anything except that God here (at the Ajna Chakra). He is seated within you, in the Sahasrara. The moment you turn your gaze inward, you will see Him; you will have the direct realization of that Supreme Being, and you will be freed from the cycle of birth and death.
Maharshi Aurobindo has described Krishna as the Supramental Force, do you understand it or not? So, this is the Sanjivani Mantra, brother. Whether you are suffering from any disease—AIDS, cancer, hepatitis B, blood cancer—start chanting this mantra. Hanuman Ji brought the Sanjivani herb.Lakshmana had become unconscious. If he had died, that would have been the end of it. But he had not died; he was only unconscious. The Sanjivani herb was given to him, and he recovered. This is the Sanjivani Mantra, brother. Whatever disease you may be suffering from, start chanting it, and you will not die from that disease—even if a doctor has said that you will not survive. Thousands have recovered, not just one—thousands. People are recovering from hepatitis B and blood cancer.
After becoming HIV-positive, no one has survived until now, and yet in this country, lakhs have survived. I have the reports on my table; they are from all over the country. They are coming to me from Bombay, understand? Bombay has treatment centers, but they are not getting cured there. Just recently, a Chinese woman came from Hong Kong; she had breast cancer. She should undergo spiritual https://t.co/OyjI0yMpdR, in this way, through meditation and chanting, all diseases will be cure.
When the Kundalini rises upward, Yoga speaks of five types of vital air: Prana, Apana, Samana, Udana, and Vyana. The kind of Pranayama you are being made to practise—Kapalabhati, whatever form it may be—there are hundreds of types of Pranayama.
Apana Vayu expels the downward discharges below the navel. The Kundalini is located in the sacrum, at the base of the spine, coiled three and a half times, with its tail held in its mouth.This will bring about a universal change. Kundalini exists in every human being, indeed in every living being, in every creature.
When it awakens, the first Bandha is formed at the Muladhara. Then the spine undergoes its own exercise, because all the systems are connected to this point here (at the Sahasrara). Then the navel will draw toward the spine. You cannot make this happen by simply willing it.
Then, as it rises further and passes above the Kanthakupa—the hollow here, below the throat—the third Bandha will be formed. This is called Jalandhara Bandha. Now, beyond this, the spine is short, and there is only a small portion left where all kinds of movement are not possible. So Pranayama takes place.
That Pranayama also happens spontaneously. You will not do it simply by willing it. There are hundreds of types of Pranayama; whichever form is needed will happen on its own. Your inner consciousness will bring it about; it will not be performed by an external Yogacharya.
In this way, as soon as the Kundalini rises above the Ajna Chakra, Samadhi will occur. Without entering Samadhi, the mystery of Nature cannot be known. And the first requirement for Samadhi is complete freedom from disease.
Now even addictions go away. Doctors are greatly surprised, and the West is greatly surprised. They say, ‘Heroin addiction will kill us,’ whereas here, even opium, heroin, and all such addictions are being given up.
That transformation, too, is taking place on a fundamental basis. Creation has arisen from Trigunamayi Maya—the three Gunas: Rajas, Tamas, and Sattva. There are Tamasik tendencies that make demands, and those demands have to be supplied. People who eat meat, drink alcohol, and so on—these Tamasik glands become active and create that demand.
Doctors asked me, ‘Guru Ji, we know that the opium addiction has gone, but what happened to the withdrawal symptoms in someone who had been consuming this poison for twenty years?
The Tamasik glands will become inactive, while the Sattvik and Rajasik tendencies will become conscious. They will not allow that tendency to arise again. The demand itself disappears. So I do not accept this argument about after-effects. This is simply a matter of demand and supply.
Once, Swami Vivekananda Ji was giving a speech in America when an American said, ‘Sir, you are giving such a long lecture, but we are not going to agree with you. In your religion, there are so many restrictions—vegetarianism, non-vegetarianism, and who knows what else. We eat meat and drink alcohol.’ So, right in the middle of his speech, Swami Ji said, ‘You need not give up these things; the things will give you up.’ You do not need to give them up; when they leave you, what will you do then?
How many people give sermons saying, ‘Do not drink alcohol. Do not consume opium.’ Does anyone listen? No one listens. They hear it through one ear and let it out through the other. Why would anyone listen to me? I say, ‘Do not give it up. If you are drinking one bottle, start drinking one and a half from today itself. But do not give up chanting the Name.’ The Name and addiction cannot go together. They cannot coexist. I have helped thousands, even hundreds of thousands, give up their addictions. So, this is the work of transforming the tendency.
In this way, transformation will come through chanting the Name and meditation. This is not some abnormal transformation. This is the evolution that is meant to take place in human beings; it has already begun. The three Koshas (Sheaths) are becoming conscious. Maharshi Aurobindo said that the knowledge attained by our Ancient Sages is returning. We have to give this knowledge to the whole world.
That is why I went to America. I said, ‘I have not come to take your dollars; I have come to donate this knowledge to you.’ Now they are perplexed because their religious identities and ideologies – their isms, come to the forefront—what is Christianity doing, what is Islam doing, what is Judaism doing? I said, ‘Hindus have never accepted the idea of religious conversion. They speak of changing the tendency.’
There is a prophecy: ‘Creation of New World.’ From this very world, new human beings will emerge. ‘Creation of New World’—and what will it be like? They say, ‘Creation of Spiritual World.
Do not tell people the mantra in this way. Tell them that all the other transformations have taken place. And there is nothing surprising about this. This is the Sanjivani Mantra. Start chanting it from now. If there is life in the person, whether it is AIDS, cancer, or hepatitis B, it will be cured—through chanting the Name alone.
Now, several AIDS cases have been cured through meditation on my photograph. But who will highlight this? The government cannot do it. In 2006, several Secretaries of the Government of India came to me in Delhi. They told me, ‘Guru Ji, the work you are doing is based on Hindu Dharma. The Middle East and the West will not allow it to continue. The government will not do it. You continue your work.’
When the Ramayana television serial was made, the Middle East strongly objected to it. But India said, ‘We have already sold the broadcasting rights.’ So I said, ‘I have no problem. I am doing my work; as long as I am alive, I will continue. The day I am gone, I am gone. But my photograph will not die.’”
Now let me tell you the Name. Just today, someone said this to me. I was told the same thing in Bangalore as well.
It is a mantra, a Beej Mantra (seed mantra), containing both the Radha and Krishna principles. The Radha principle gives worldly enjoyment, while the Krishna principle gives liberation. Thus, worldly enjoyment and liberation go together in this mantra. In other forms of worship, if there is worldly enjoyment, there is no liberation; if there is liberation, there is no worldly enjoyment. One has to renounce one of the two.
There is one syllable: ‘Kleeng,’ the syllable ‘Kleeng.’ In Bangalore too, I was told that many people pronounce it ‘Kleem.’ Do not pronounce it ‘Kleem.’ There is the Hindi vowel ‘a’; as soon as a dot (bindu) is placed above it, what does it become? ‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng’—‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng,’ ‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng,’ ‘Kleeng Krishna Kleeng.’
And to the press and media people, I make a request: this is an off-the-record matter. Print whatever else you wish, but do not print the mantra.
The cycle of coming and going will come to an end; you will be freed from the cycle of birth and death.
Kalki Avatar Sadguru Shri Ramlal Ji Siyag

2026 𝙒𝙞𝙨𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙨𝙞𝙣 𝙁𝙖𝙡𝙡 𝙀𝙡𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣 𝙂𝙪𝙞𝙙𝙚

With early In-Person Absentee Voting starting today (visit the link in the comments for more information. If you are in Germantown, as I am, voting will take place at Village Hall), it’s time once again for my biannual voter guide. As those of you who follow Wisconsin politics know all too well, Wisconsin voters don’t get to take time off. Every election in the state feels like the most important election of our lives. And every election in the state IS the most important election of our lives, at least until the next one… except for maybe this one.

Why? Because, for the first time since 2010, Wisconsin has a chance to move FORWARD once again. The past sixteen years have been difficult. Republicans have decimated the once-famous "Laboratory of Democracy” built by legendary Wisconsin heroes like Fighting Bob LaFollette, and turned it into the Koch Brothers’ playhouse, a place to test their worst, most publicly destructive policies, with the support of vile miscreants like Scott Walker. Walker employed his “divide and conquer” strategy to turn public and private unions against one another (the rich and powerful will do whatever they can to trick the working class into fighting with itself). He planned to systematically dismantle organized labor in Wisconsin at the behest of his billionaire backers who long sought to attack workers’ rights and protections to increase their wealth and power.

The state that birthed “the Wisconsin Idea”, the first state in the union to enshrine workmen’s compensation, the first state to have an unemployment insurance program, the first state to recognize collective bargaining rights for public employees, was now preparing its demise. Beginning with Act 10, right-wing billionaire-puppet Scott Walker ended collective bargaining rights for public employee unions (exempting traditionally conservative unions like Police and sheriff's deputies). Act 10 also made it significantly more difficult to certify and maintain a union, leading to a 29% decrease in public sector union membership rate (46.6% down to a measly 18.5%), and shifted financial burden (retirement and healthcare contributions) onto employees, leading to an exodus of dedicated, talented public servants. Then, four years later, Walker passed “Right to Work”, a classic right-wing misnomer designed to imply the opposite of what it actually does. Like saying the “Patriot Act” (the most invasive, expansive, and unconstitutional advancement of mass surveillance in history) was meant to expand freedom when, in reality, it massively infringes on personal privacy rights and constitutional protections. “Right to Work” is touted as a way to increase worker freedom and choice when, in reality, it significantly weakens workers' bargaining power.

Scott Walker and his billionaire buddies did everything they could to weaken worker power in the state, and they succeeded. And I haven’t even touched on his attacks on the environment, consumer protections, disability rights, immigrant rights, local control, public schools, elections, women’s health, nor his massive corporate tax cuts. And don’t get me started on the secrecy agreements Republican lawmakers signed so that Scott Walker could sign aggressively gerrymandered maps, considered the worst in the nation after receiving an “F” from the Princeton Gerrymandering Project. Since 2011, Wisconsin has experienced a dramatic increase in child poverty rates, nonexistent wage growth, steep cuts to K-through-12 public schools and the state university system, and a significant decline in water quality, per Dan Kaufman, author of “The Fall of Wisconsin: The Conservative Conquest of a Progressive Bastion and the Future of American Politics”. Under Republican leadership, Wisconsin has fallen backward. Scott Walker is a sleazebag. His legacy reflects that.

But all of that can change come November. We have a chance to flip the Wisconsin Legislature and, when we do, Wisconsin will reclaim its mantle as the most “Forward”-thinking state in the country. The Legislature alone isn’t enough, however. We also have to retain the Governor’s Mansion. When we secure the Trifecta, we will signal to the nation that Wisconsin is restoring our progressive roots, reclaiming our progressive history, and redefining our progressive future. As goes Wisconsin, so goes the nation.
Here I will lay out WHAT decisions I have made and WHY I feel each choice is best. Election day, Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026, is two weeks away. Our vote is our voice, and we all deserve to be heard! Talk to your friends, family, neighbors, etc. and MAKE SURE everyone has a plan to vote. Early voting is incredibly easy, I highly suggest it if election day does not work for your schedule.

This guide will be in the order of each race on my ballot, covering only races I have on my ballot. To see an example of what your ballot will look like, visit myvote.wi (.gov) and click “What’s On My Ballot”.
Starting from the top of (my) ballot, we begin with…
—----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
𝙂𝙤𝙫𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙤𝙧 / 𝙇𝙞𝙚𝙪𝙩𝙚𝙣𝙖𝙣𝙩 𝙂𝙤𝙫𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙤𝙧- 𝘿𝙖𝙫𝙞𝙙 𝘾𝙧𝙤𝙬𝙡𝙚𝙮/𝙎𝙖𝙧𝙖𝙝 𝙂𝙤𝙙𝙡𝙚𝙬𝙨𝙠𝙞

Those who know me, and have followed my content, are very well aware of my stance in the Gubernatorial Primary. While the results did not go the way that I had hoped, the democratic process is sacrosanct. But, friends, we still have a damn good choice here. I won’t get everything I wanted from Governor @DavidCCrowley, but I will get most of what I wanted. More importantly, I’m getting a Governor who will listen to his constituents and understands the importance of compromise. A Governor that will fight for working-class people instead of his three billionaire donors. A Governor that we can work with (and pressure when necessary) to enact the desperately necessary progressive policies this state hungers for. As he has done throughout his career. In particular, David’s support for $20 for ‘26, a Living Wage for Wisconsin is of immense importance to me. All work has value, all labor has dignity, all Wisconsinites deserve a living wage. We can put money in the pockets of 800,000 working Wisconsinites, helping families put a roof over their heads, food on their tables, and maybe a nice trip to the Dells now and then, or a weekend at the Zoo or the movies, time permitting. The working-class is struggling. The rich are getting richer, the rest of us are falling further and further behind. This is an opportunity to tangibly improve the lives of 1 out of 5 working Wisconsinites. Money that will go right back into our communities (instead of being sent to some overseas Cayman Islands account) to grow Wisconsin’s economy. Wages are a policy choice, wages represent leverage.
